acceptance.given: A Package A validator or test invocation contract is defined.

oracle.expected: The invocation uses a literal argv vector and a finite positive caller-supplied timeout.
forbidden: A shell string is treated as the machine command contract.
An invocation has no finite positive caller-assigned timeout.
oracle.observable: Invocation construction and timeout assignment are inspectable in the implementation and targeted tests.

acceptance.then: The invocation contract records argv and a finite positive timeout.
acceptance.when: Inspecting or executing a validator or test invocation

failure_intents.selector_intent: A planned pytest selector raises AssertionError when invocation construction uses a shell string or lacks a finite positive caller timeout.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Use literal argv vectors and finite positive caller-assigned timeouts for Package A invocations.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert invocation-contract checks while retaining the documented CLI contract.

slice_hint.state_transition: Invocation definitions become explicit argv plus finite positive timeout contracts.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Targeted and terminal tests reject shell-string commands and missing, zero, negative, or unbounded timeouts.

acceptance.given: Package A public CLI invocation guidance is documented.

oracle.expected: The guidance identifies python as the active interpreter and py -3 -B as the Windows option.
forbidden: The documented invocation requires a non-active interpreter or excludes the stated Windows form.
oracle.observable: The published standard contains both interpreter forms in its public invocation guidance.

acceptance.then: The documentation explicitly names python and py -3 -B.
acceptance.when: Reviewing the Package A standard and public CLI documentation

failure_intents.selector_intent: A documentation-contract selector raises AssertionError when either required interpreter form is absent.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Document active python usage and the equivalent Windows py -3 -B form.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore prior documentation while preserving validator behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Public CLI guidance gains explicit active-interpreter and Windows-equivalent forms.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The documentation test finds both required forms in the published standard.

acceptance.given: ADR-0062 is being drafted with an explicit lifecycle status.

oracle.expected: The ADR remains Proposed until normal maintainer acceptance and is cited as new authority only after acceptance.
forbidden: A draft ADR is cited as accepted implementation authority before maintainer acceptance.
A draft ADR is marked Accepted solely to satisfy a test.
oracle.observable: ADR-0062 status and ADR index references consistently show proposal and acceptance gating.

acceptance.then: Governance records preserve Proposed status during drafting and gate authority citations on acceptance.
acceptance.when: Reviewing or updating ADR-0062 and its index entry

failure_intents.selector_intent: A governance-document selector raises AssertionError when ADR-0062 is prematurely Accepted or cited as accepted authority without maintainer decision.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Record ADR-0062 as Proposed during drafting and require normal maintainer acceptance before authority citation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert ADR index lifecycle edits without changing existing accepted ADR authority.

slice_hint.state_transition: ADR-0062 gains explicit Proposed status and acceptance-gated authority references.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Governance checks reject premature acceptance or authority citation.

acceptance.given: Package A scope is defined by its frozen negative-scope list and declared allowlists.

oracle.expected: No excluded capability, system, analysis, installation behavior, or mandatory internal review is added to Package A.
forbidden: Any of the named capabilities or systems is added as Package A scope.
oracle.observable: A scope-boundary check compares Package A deliverables and declarations against the explicit exclusion list.

acceptance.then: Implementation and declarations remain within the explicit negative scope list.
acceptance.when: Reviewing Package A design, deliverables, and scope-boundary validation

failure_intents.selector_intent: A scope-boundary selector raises AssertionError when a Package A declaration or deliverable introduces an excluded capability, system, analysis, installation behavior, or mandatory review.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce the frozen Package A negative-scope boundary across declarations and implementation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Remove scope-boundary additions while preserving existing validator result compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Package A declarations and implementation become constrained to the frozen allowlist and exclusions.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Scope-boundary tests reject every excluded addition and protected-path introduction.
